description: Use this when the user wants a new CSV file from a table, for example "put this table in a CSV", "make a spreadsheet file from these rows", "export this list as CSV for Excel". Input tips: pass columns (header names) and rows, where each row has exactly one cell per column (text, number, true, false or null for empty). Example: columns ["name","city"], rows [["Ada","London"],["Linus","Helsinki"]]. Up to 2,000 rows and 100 columns. Optional: filename, excel_bom (true when the user opens it in Excel and the text has accents) and escape_formulas (show cells starting with = + - or @ as text). Returns: the CSV text, a download link that works for 24 hours, its expiry, the row count and byte size. Not for: opening, reading, editing or adding up an existing spreadsheet or .xlsx file; it only writes a new CSV. Errors: status invalid with a message naming the row and cell to fix.

columns.description: Header names in order, such as ["name","city","note"].

escape_formulas.description: Prefix text cells that start with = + - or @ with an apostrophe so a spreadsheet shows them as text. Default false.

excel_bom.description: Start the file with a UTF-8 byte order mark so Excel opens accents correctly. Default false.

filename.description: File name in letters and digits, such as contacts; .csv is added.

rows.description: Up to 2000 rows, such as [["Ada","London","first program"]]. Each row has exactly one cell per column. An empty list gives a header-only file.

items.description: One row. Its cell count must equal the number of columns; use null for an empty cell.

name: make_csv_file

bytes.description: Size of the downloadable file in bytes, with the byte order mark when excel_bom is true.

csv_text.description: The CSV text (RFC 4180, CRLF line ends) when status is ok, without the byte order mark.

download_url.description: Link that works for 24 hours, or null when no link could be made.

expires_at.description: When the link stops working (ISO 8601 UTC).

filename.description: Name the download link saves the file as, such as calendar.ics.

message.description: What to fix in the input when status is invalid.

notes.description: Facts the user should know, such as how long the link works.

rows.description: Number of data rows, not counting the header.

status.description: ok when the file was made; invalid when the input needs a fix (see message).

title: Make a CSV file
